liveProviderEvidence.conclusion: The workload identity reached the atomic grant consumer, but no exact grant existed. The broker denied access as intended, while its separate denial-audit RPC failed with HTTP 403 and persisted no attempt row.

sourceOnlyRemediation.brokerBehavior: A grant miss now returns a 503 audit failure unless the denial-audit RPC succeeds; it returns GRANT_NOT_AVAILABLE only after audit persistence succeeds.
sourceOnlyRemediation.authorizationBoundary: The replacement is one explicit transaction, uses a shared function-writer advisory lock plus an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE table lock, and refuses unknown drift through exact old/new function hashes, complete ACL and effective-access assertions, permanent-table and replica-identity assertions, exact table/column/constraint/index hashes, and policy/trigger/rule checks. It retains the postgres-owned SECURITY DEFINER function with empty search_path, revokes public/anon/authenticated execution, and grants execution only to service_role. It removes the redundant request JWT claim test that rejected the modern secret-key call even though the function ACL already admitted only service_role/postgres.
sourceOnlyRemediation.workflowDiagnostics: For broker HTTP denials the unattended workflow prints only a bounded uppercase error code and HTTP status. For broker transport failure it prints the fixed BROKER_REQUEST_FAILED code and HTTP 000. It never prints the response message or success token.
